answer: A score bound to the key that earned it resists sybils: it cannot be sold, merged, or delegated. A cluster inherits nothing from its operator's history, so all N fresh keys start at zero and must each build a separate record; attacker cost scales linearly while an honest operator pays once. Scores also cannot be pooled into one credible identity: each identity is an island with no bridge out, a high scorer is a mesa that cannot level newcomers by import, and every new key must relight its own lantern. Payout reads per-key history only, so inflating identity count gains nothing.
